item.title: Pakistan rules out talks with Afghanistan as fighting enters third day
item.description:
Pakistan and Afghanistan continued to exchange fire along their contested border on Saturday, with Islamabad ruling out negotiations and demanding Kabul end its alleged support for militant groups, as the most serious military confrontation between the two neighbors in years showed no signs of abating.

Pakistan's prime minister's spokesperson told Pakistani television on Saturday that "there won't be talks" and "there's no negotiation," insisting Afghanistan must first cease harboring militants. The statement came despite the Taliban government expressing willingness to resolve the crisis through dialogue. The European Union's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas also urged both nations Saturday to lower tensions, warning the violence could destabilize the wider region.

item.title: Airport deaths reported as Iran retaliates for US-Israeli strikes
item.description:
Coordinated military strikes by the United States and Israel against Iran on Saturday, February 28, brought commercial aviation across the Middle East to a near-standstill, stranding tens of thousands of travelers worldwide and forcing airlines from every continent to cancel, divert, or reroute flights.

At least eight countries — Iran, Israel, Iraq, Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, Jordan, and the United Arab Emirates — closed their airspace in the hours following the strikes, which began around 1:15 a.m. EST. Flight tracking data from Flightradar24 showed the skies over much of the region virtually empty of commercial traffic by Saturday afternoon. Preliminary data from aviation analytics firm Cirium, cited by Reuters, indicated that nearly 40 percent of flights to Dubai and a comparable share of flights to the wider region were cancelled on Saturday alone.

item.title: Regional toll mounts as Iran and Israel trade strikes through the day
item.description:
Iran launched waves of ballistic missiles and drones at Israel and multiple Gulf Arab nations on Saturday, hours after the United States and Israel began a joint military offensive against Iranian targets that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and struck military and nuclear sites across the country.

The Iranian counterattack targeted not only Israel but also US military bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Jordan, marking one of the broadest regional escalations in decades. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps vowed the strikes would continue "until the enemy is conclusively vanquished".

item.title: Iran forms temporary leadership council after Khamenei killed in US-Israeli strikes
item.description:
Iran has set in motion its constitutional succession process after state television confirmed that Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed during coordinated US-Israeli airstrikes on Saturday, marking the most profound rupture in the Islamic Republic since its founding nearly five decades ago.

A temporary leadership council composed of President Masoud Pezeshkian, judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei, and a jurist member of the Guardian Council — selected by the Expediency Discernment Council — has assumed the duties of the supreme leader, according to Iranian state news agency IRNA. Mohammad Mokhber, one of Khamenei's advisers, confirmed in a televised interview that the transition was being carried out under Article 111 of Iran's constitution, which governs the interim period following a supreme leader's death.

item.title: Iran faces leadership vacuum after Khamenei killed in U.S.-Israeli strikes
item.description:
The killing of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Saturday has plunged the Islamic Republic into its deepest leadership crisis since the 1979 revolution, with no clear successor and competing factions already maneuvering for power.

Iranian state television and the state-run IRNA news agency confirmed the 86-year-old's death early Sunday, following what President Donald Trump described as "major combat operations" launched alongside Israel against Iranian military and government targets. Trump called the moment "the single greatest chance for the Iranian people to take back their Country".

item.title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz after U.S.-Israeli strikes kill Khamenei
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared the Strait of Hormuz closed to all maritime traffic on Saturday, broadcasting warnings over naval radio that no ships would be permitted to transit the waterway, according to Reuters. The move came hours after the United States and Israel launched joint military strikes against Iran in what President Donald Trump called "major combat operations," an operation dubbed "Epic Fury".

item.title: Iran threatens Strait of Hormuz blockade after U.S., Israeli strikes
item.description: The United States and Israel launched a wave of airstrikes against Iran early Saturday, triggering a chain of events that threatens to upend global energy markets when trading resumes. Iran's Revolutionary Guards have warned that "no ship is allowed to pass the Strait of Hormuz," according to an official with the EU naval mission Aspides cited by Reuters, while satellite data from MarineTraffic showed a sharp decline in vessel traffic through the waterway over the weekend.

item.title: OPEC+ weighs emergency output boost as Hormuz shipping grinds to a halt
item.description: The joint US and Israeli military assault on Iran that began Saturday has thrown global energy markets into turmoil, with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — the chokepoint for roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil — grinding to a near halt as traders brace for a potentially historic price spike when markets reopen Sunday evening.

item.title: Brent crude surges to $80 as Iran conflict shuts Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Brent crude surged roughly 10 percent to about $80 a barrel in off-market transactions on Sunday, as U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran threw global energy markets into turmoil and effectively shut down one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints.

The spike came as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a narrow waterway responsible for more than 20 percent of global oil transit — ground to a halt after Iran's Revolutionary Guards contacted vessels to declare the strait closed. Iranian state television reported that an oil tanker attempting to pass through the strait was struck and was sinking, broadcasting footage of a burning vessel at sea.

item.title: 3 US service members killed in Iran operation, CENTCOM says
item.description: US Central Command confirmed on the morning of March 1 that three American service members have been killed in action and five others seriously wounded during Operation Epic Fury, the ongoing joint US-Israeli military campaign against Iran. The deaths mark the first American combat fatalities since the operation began on February 28.

item.title: US calls Iran's claim it struck USS Lincoln a 'lie'
item.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed on Sunday that it struck the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln with four ballistic missiles in the Persian Gulf, a claim the US military swiftly and forcefully rejected as a "LIE."

The IRGC issued the claim as part of what Tehran calls Operation True Promise 4, a retaliatory campaign following joint US and Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. If confirmed, the strike would have marked the first direct hit on a US aircraft carrier in decades. But US Central Command left no room for ambiguity.

item.title: CIA tracked Khamenei for months before Israel struck Tehran
item.description:
The CIA monitored Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's movements for months before identifying a rare gathering of Iran's top political and military leaders at a government compound in central Tehran on Saturday morning, providing the intelligence that enabled Israel to launch a precision strike killing Khamenei and more than 40 senior officials, according to reports from The New York Times citing people familiar with the operation.

The agency passed what officials described as "high fidelity" intelligence on Khamenei's location to Israel, prompting U.S. and Israeli forces to accelerate the timing of a joint military campaign that had been weeks in planning. The breakthrough came when CIA sources learned that Khamenei would be present at the compound alongside senior security aides for a Saturday morning meeting, rather than the evening session originally expected.

item.title: Death toll at Iranian girls' school rises to 148
item.description:
A missile strike on a girls' elementary school in the southern Iranian city of Minab emerged as the deadliest single incident of the joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran, with the death toll climbing from an initial count of 108 reported by the Iranian Red Crescent to 148 according to the local prosecutor, as cited by Iranian state media and confirmed by The Wall Street Journal and CNN.

The strike hit the Shajareh Tayyebeh all-girls primary school at approximately 10:45 a.m. local time on Saturday, February 28, as roughly 170 students between the ages of seven and 12 were attending class during what is a regular school day in Iran. The impact destroyed the building's walls and caused its roof to collapse, burying students underneath the rubble. Verified footage showed thick black smoke rising from a structure adorned with pastel-painted flowers, as rescuers used cranes and shovels to reach those trapped inside.

item.title: Iran's foreign minister vows 'no limit' to self-defense after Khamenei killed
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Sunday that Iran sees "no limit" to its right to self-defense following the assassination of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in coordinated US-Israeli strikes, rejecting President Donald Trump's warnings against retaliation and framing the military response as a matter of national survival.

item.title: ESA releases new images of interstellar comet ahead of Jupiter flyby
item.description:
The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, the third object ever confirmed to have entered our solar system from beyond, is heading for a close encounter with Jupiter on March 16, when it will pass within 33 million miles of the gas giant. The flyby marks one of the final observable milestones before the ancient visitor disappears into the void of interstellar space.

First detected in July 2025 by a NASA-funded ATLAS telescope in Chile, the comet has captivated astronomers with its extraordinary speed — clocked at 137,000 miles per hour — and a hyperbolic trajectory confirming it could not have originated in our solar system. Only two interstellar objects had previously been identified: 1I/'Oumuamua in 2017 and 2I/Borisov in 2019.

item.title: Trump says he agreed to talk with Iran as strikes continue
item.description: The United States and Israel launched a massive joint military operation against Iran on February 28, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of senior military and political leaders in what the Pentagon dubbed "Operation Epic Fury" and Israel codenamed "Roaring Lion." Iran responded with retaliatory missile and drone strikes across the Middle East, targeting Israel and U.S. military bases in at least six countries, killing three American service members and raising fears of a wider regional war.

item.title: Major shipping firms halt Suez Canal transit after strikes on Iran
item.description:
A.P. Moller-Maersk announced on Sunday that it will halt all sailings through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal, rerouting vessels around the Cape of Good Hope after U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran plunged the region's key maritime chokepoints into crisis. The decision reverses the Danish shipping giant's recent move to resume transit through the Red Sea corridor, which had been disrupted by Houthi rebel attacks since late 2023.

"Due to the deteriorating security situation in the Middle East region following the escalating military conflict, we have decided to pause future Trans-Suez sailings through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait for the time being," Maersk said in a statement.

item.title: Trump says Iran war could last four weeks as combat operations intensify
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Sunday that U.S. military operations in Iran will continue "in full force" until all American objectives are met, as the joint U.S.-Israeli campaign entered its second day with mounting casualties on all sides and retaliatory strikes reverberating across the Middle East.

In a video posted to Truth Social, Trump acknowledged the deaths of three American service members and warned that more losses are likely. "Combat operations continue at this time in full force, and they will continue until all of our objectives are achieved," he said, pledging to "avenge" the fallen troops. In a phone interview with the Daily Mail, Trump offered the clearest timeline yet for the campaign, saying, "It's always been a four-week process. We figured it will be four weeks or so. It's a big country. It'll take four weeks — or less".

item.title: Trump confirms three US troops killed as he warns more may follow
item.description:
President Donald Trump acknowledged Sunday that three American service members had been killed during the U.S.-Israeli military offensive against Iran and warned that more casualties were likely as combat operations continue. "We have three casualties, but we expect more; ultimately, this will lead to a significant outcome for the world," Trump told NBC News.

The deaths, announced by U.S. Central Command at 9:30 a.m. ET on March 1, mark the first confirmed American fatalities since the joint operation — dubbed Operation Epic Fury — began early Saturday. Five additional service members were seriously wounded, while several others sustained minor shrapnel injuries and concussions and were returning to duty, CENTCOM said in a post on X.

item.title: Canada's Carney arrives in Delhi for Modi talks amid Iran crisis
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney landed in New Delhi on Saturday as part of a three-nation tour aimed at deepening trade ties with Indo-Pacific partners, even as U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran and Tehran's retaliatory attacks across the Middle East cast a shadow over global diplomacy.
